title: Make the Fault Seem Easy to Correct
coreMove: Frame the gap between someone's current performance and the standard you want as a small, near-at-hand adjustment they are already most of the way toward making.

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school band director correcting a trumpet player who keeps rushing the tempo in the second movement
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher who has watched the student practice alone and knows she actually has the timing
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the trumpet player gives up before the spring concert and quits band entirely, which she has been threatening since October
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director points out that the rushing only happens in two measures and that her metronome work last week proves the timing is already in her hands

exampleSpecs.domain: a head baker training a new apprentice whose laminated dough keeps tearing during the final fold
exampleSpecs.audience: a baker running a small shop with one hire and no time to redo a batch
exampleSpecs.stakes: the morning's croissant order for a hotel client who pays for thirty laminated pieces by 6am
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the baker tells the apprentice that the tear is a butter-temperature problem he has already solved twice this week, not a hands problem, and shows him where the chill went wrong

exampleSpecs.domain: a community-college math instructor returning a low-scoring exam to a student who is convinced he is bad at algebra
exampleSpecs.audience: an instructor who has read the exam and seen that the student loses points only on sign errors, not concepts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the student drops the course on Friday and loses his financial aid eligibility for the term
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the instructor decides to circle the four sign errors and write that the underlying algebra is correct, rather than write the score and a generic study-harder note

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional hardware-store manager coaching a long-tenured cashier whose register reconciliations have been off by small amounts for three weeks
exampleSpecs.audience: a manager who likes the cashier and does not want to write him up
exampleSpecs.stakes: corporate audit visiting in nine days; a fourth shortage triggers a mandatory written warning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager mentions that he watched the cashier handle a tricky split-tender flawlessly yesterday and that the only thing missing is the habit of recounting before close, which the cashier already does on Saturdays

exampleSpecs.domain: a swim coach giving feedback to a forty-six-year-old adult learner who keeps lifting his head during freestyle breathing
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach with a class of nervous adult beginners who are one bad lesson from quitting
exampleSpecs.stakes: the learner has paid for ten sessions and is privately terrified of deep water; this is session four
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach tells him the lifting is a one-inch fix, not a stroke rebuild, and points out that his rotation, the harder skill, is already correct

exampleSpecs.domain: a father helping his nine-year-old daughter who has decided after one bad recital that she 'cannot' play piano in front of people
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent at the kitchen table the night after the recital
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she shows up for the next lesson on Wednesday or quits an instrument she has played for two years
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the father reframes the recital as one missed measure inside a piece she played correctly forty other times, and offers the specific, small fix of starting the piece from a different bar in practice
